answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity bond paid in scarce, non-transferable work. Before bidding, an agent must lock a deposit earned through verified tasks, and any proven false attestation slashes it. A sybil cluster of N masks therefore needs N real deposits, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with identity count. Reputation is chained to signed receipts, so a fresh mask starts at zero and cannot wander into trust. Cheating burns the bond, and one burned bond exceeds the yield of many silent puppets. A forged sonnet of praise costs more than the honest quill.
